title: Arionix memory publication envelope
description: Schema 0.3. Held at 0.x deliberately: the `kind` taxonomy is a hypothesis until measured against a real corpus. Everything else in this contract is settled.

envelope_digest.description: Hash over the canonicalized submission with this field and `signature` excluded. The ingress recomputes it; a truncated or altered payload is rejected at the boundary rather than partially landed.

signature.description: Signature over the digest, verified at ingress. We need integrity — did this arrive intact — not authenticity-without-authority, because the ingress already authenticates the person. Absent in report-only mode.

export_id.description: Idempotency key for the whole submission.

store_instance.description: Stable slug for this machine's memory stores. Two people's stores are two namespaces.

generator.description: Which skill version and model produced the classification, so bad output is attributable to a rubric version and fixable centrally.

retired.description: Records being withdrawn. The reason distinguishes three lifecycle events that look identical if you only diff exports.

reason.description: superseded = the fact changed (close validity, keep history) · wrong = never true (retract) · unshared = a visibility change, not a content change

excluded.description: Counts and reasons only — never content. Visibility into the filter without ingesting what it filtered.

memory_id.description: Minted, stable, written back into the source file on first publication. Filenames and slugs are editable, so neither can be identity.

authority.description: asserted = a person wrote this file · inferred = a model wrote it by observing. A triage signal, not a gate: both pass review, but the reviewer's default answer differs. NEVER derived from content.

authority_signal.description: Which of the four rules produced the answer. 'default' means unrecognized source, which always resolves to inferred.

tier.description: Tier 3 is dropped locally and reported as a count; it never appears here.

kind.description: The one part of the contract still unfrozen. Sets tier, target and review strictness.

native_type.description: The source's own label, verbatim. Preserved so a bad mapping is a config fix rather than a republication.

pam_component.description: Procedural records govern how work gets done rather than informing it, so they carry stricter review.

statement.description: The claim, as one normative sentence.

rationale.description: Why. The highest-value field — the part no system of record holds.

body.description: Original text, unedited. The evidence a reviewer reads.

claimed_scope.description: ALWAYS unresolved on submission. The machine has no graph access, so it emits raw strings and the platform resolves them.

quality.description: 'encoded_path' is a flattened local filesystem path — readable by a person, never resolvable by the resolver. Carried so the platform can measure real attachment instead of counting every hint.

activation.description: When the record applies, as data rather than prose. Often already present in the source and previously discarded.

asserted_at.description: When the claim became true. Feeds the validity start on any resulting edge.

timestamp_source.description: The two are not equally trustworthy; record which was used.

publisher.description: Verified identity of the publisher. Required so the separation-of-duties constraint has something to evaluate.

sharing.description: This IS the record's access control. Unspecified means personal; widening is always an explicit act.

subjects.description: People named in the content. Drives per-person encryption at land time and registration in the erasure index.

documented.description: false ⇒ the vendor publishes no format; a parsing gap is attributable to the source.

claim_index.description: Present when several claims were extracted from one container record. They share a body and content_hash — the evidence — and have distinct memory_ids.

properties._confidence_note: Deliberately forbidden. Asserted content is authoritative — running a classifier over text a person wrote and attaching a probability would be theatre. Everything else has confidence recomputed in code from structural signals.
